title: NC Religious Freedom Restoration Act
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill creates the North Carolina Religious Freedom Restoration Act, which requires state and local government actions to meet strict legal standards when they burden religious practice. It also protects religious gatherings in homes and neighborhoods from housing restrictions, and ensures religious institutions receive equal treatment during emergencies.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill protects religious freedom by preventing neutral government laws from inadvertently restricting worship practices. They contend it provides necessary legal protection for religious individuals and institutions, ensures religious gatherings in homes cannot be restricted by local rules or homeowner associations, and guarantees religious organizations are treated the same as other entities during emergencies.
aiConArguments: Opponents worry the bill's broad definitions of religious burden and exemptions could override public health, safety, and anti-discrimination laws. They express concern that the strict scrutiny standard and attorney's fees provision could enable religious exemptions from generally applicable rules, potentially harm vulnerable groups, and create uncertainty about which laws can be enforced fairly and uniformly across the population.
